welcome_lead: Profit on paper isn't enough — you need cash in hand. 💸

concepts.def: Money moving in and out over time
Bank lets you spend more than you have

walkthroughs.body_html:
Cash flow is the timing of money in and out.

You might make a profit on a big order — but if the customer pays in 90 days, your wages are due tomorrow. 😬

Inflows = sales, loans, investor money.

Outflows = wages, rent, stock, tax.

Net cash flow = inflow − outflow. Positive is good; negative is danger.

If a business can't pay its bills, it is insolvent and may close — even if it's profitable!

Solutions:

  • Use an overdraft.
  • Ask customers to pay faster.
  • Ask suppliers to wait longer.
  • Cut costs or delay buying stock.

mcqs.q: Why does a company's share price change?
options: Share prices are set by the government each morning.
Share prices reflect investors' expectations about future profits — driven by company performance, sector trends, economic conditions, and market sentiment.
Porter's strategies are about marketing channels.
Share prices go up when a company makes more money this year.

mcqs.q: What are Porter's two main generic strategies for competitive advantage?
options: Porter's strategies are about marketing channels.
Cost leadership (being the lowest-cost producer) and differentiation (offering unique value customers will pay more for) — Porter argues firms should choose one or the other.
Porter says businesses should pursue both low cost and differentiation at once.
